fact: A standard professional football match lasts for 90 minutes, split into two equal halves of 45 minutes each.
Brazil is the most successful nation in FIFA World Cup history, having won the tournament 5 times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).
The first ever FIFA World Cup took place in Uruguay in 1930, with Uruguay emerging as champions after defeating Argentina 4-2.
Only the goalkeeper is allowed to intentionally touch the football with their hands or arms during open play, and only within their own penalty area.
Cristiano Ronaldo holds the world record for the most international goals scored by an individual in men's football.
Real Madrid holds the record for the most UEFA Champions League / European Cup titles in history.
Lionel Messi holds the record for the most Ballon d'Or awards won by a player in history, with 8 titles.
The penalty spot in standard association football is located exactly 12 yards (11 meters) away from the center of the goal line.
Miroslav Klose of Germany holds the record for the most goals scored in FIFA World Cup tournament history with 16 goals across four tournaments.
Arsenal completed the entire 2003-04 Premier League season undefeated (26 wins, 12 draws), earning the moniker 'The Invincibles'.
According to IFAB Law 11, a player is not in an offside position if they receive the ball directly from a throw-in, corner kick, or goal kick.
Leicester City won the English Premier League in the 2015-16 season with pre-season betting odds of 5000-to-1.
Just Fontaine of France holds the record for the most goals scored in a single FIFA World Cup tournament, netting 13 goals in the 1958 World Cup in Sweden.
Sheffield FC, founded on October 24, 1857 in England, is officially recognized by FIFA as the world's oldest existing football club.
Sadio Mane scored the fastest hat-trick in Premier League history, netting 3 goals in 2 minutes and 56 seconds for Southampton against Aston Villa in 2015.
Under IFAB Law 12, an indirect free kick is awarded if a goalkeeper controls the ball with their hands for more than six seconds before releasing it.
The 1950 World Cup decisive match at Maracana Stadium between Uruguay and Brazil had an estimated unofficial attendance of 199,854 spectators, the highest in football history.
Rogerio Ceni, a Brazilian goalkeeper for Sao Paulo, scored 131 career goals through free kicks and penalties, the highest by any goalkeeper in football history.
